judges: Sanjay K. Agrawal C.A.V. Judgment J.

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Suddu Ram, aged about 45 years, S/o late Ghasiram Gond
parties.respondent_defendant: Kamlesh Kumar, aged about 19 years, S/o Ganga Prasad Halwa, and others

facts_of_case: The plaintiff's second appeal was filed against the finding of the trial court holding that the appellant/plaintiff is not the legal son of Ghasiram. The plaintiff claimed to have entered into marriage with Ghasi in chudi form during the lifetime of Dulli and sought a share in the suit property.

legal_principles.principle: Children born out of a void marriage are entitled to inherit the self-acquired property of their parents.
legal_principles.held: though would be branded as illegitimate son of Ghasi, would still be entitled to inherit the self-acquired property of Ghasi and he will be treated as legitimate for all practical purposes including succession.

legal_principles.principle: A legal fiction can be created to treat illegitimate children as legitimate for succession purposes.
legal_principles.held: it is by a rule of fictio juris that the legislature has provided that children, though illegitimate, shall, nevertheless, be treated as legitimate notwithstanding that the marriage was void or voidable.
cited_cases: Parayankandiyal Eravath Kanapravan Kalliani Amma (Smt) and others v. K. Devi and others
J.K. Cotton Spg. & Wvg. Mills Ltd. v. Union of India
American Home Products Corpn. v. Mac Laboratories (P) Ltd.
